definition: HeyGen is a generative artificial intelligence company that creates photo-realistic avatars via user-submitted photos and videos as well as a library of pre-made avatars and voices.
details: The digital avatar can recite prompts in multiple languages. When submitting content to be used in the generation of a video, users are required to give verbal consent, along with a spoken password to verify their identity. Human moderators are used to remove and block any content used for the purpose of bullying, harassment, and the spread of disinformation, in addition to the use of an automated content filter.

explainer.lead: HeyGen turns a script and an avatar into a video of a digital person speaking, with support for multiple languages. It can create presenter-style videos without filming a speaker each time, while using consent checks and moderation to constrain misuse.

tiers.eli5: HeyGen is like a digital puppet that can speak the words you give it. You can make an avatar from your own photos and videos, or choose a ready-made avatar and voice. If you use your own media, you must say that you agree and speak a password so the system can check your identity.
tiers.practitioner: A typical workflow is to select or create an avatar, supply a prompt, and generate a video of the avatar reciting it in the chosen language. User-submitted media requires verbal consent and a spoken password for identity verification. Plan for both automated filtering and human moderation, particularly around harassment, bullying, and disinformation.
tiers.paperLevel: The system can be described as a mapping from avatar assets, voice, prompt, and language to a speaking-avatar video, using either user-submitted media or pre-made assets. For user-submitted media, verbal consent and a spoken password gate generation. Output governance combines automated content filtering with human moderation, so prohibited content is not handled by generation constraints alone.

explainer.example: A user submits their own photos and videos, gives verbal consent, and speaks the required password. They then enter a short training script and generate versions in which their photo-realistic avatar recites it in English and Spanish.

usedIn.name: Pre-made avatar videos

explainer.intuition: Instead of recording a person for every script, HeyGen combines a digital presenter with a prompt and generates the presenter speaking it.
howItWorks: Choose a pre-made avatar and voice, or submit photos and videos for a custom avatar.
For user-submitted media, provide verbal consent and speak a password to verify your identity.
Enter the prompt you want the avatar to recite and choose among its supported languages.
Automated filtering and human moderators address prohibited content and misuse.
explainer.whyItMatters: It makes spoken video presentation repeatable and multilingual without requiring a new recording for every prompt. Its consent, identity-verification, and moderation steps also show safeguards being built directly into an avatar-generation workflow.
misconceptions: It is not limited to avatars made from a user's own appearance; pre-made avatars and voices are also available.
Submitting personal media does not bypass consent and identity checks.
Content safety is not handled only by an automated filter; human moderators are also used.
